title: Stripe prefetcher and per-CPU pin highways for block manager
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Reduce early-warmup p99 tails and allocator contention in the paged KV block manager for mixed small/large request patterns. Current freelist grabs and opportunistic prefetch lead to head-of-line contention on high core counts and bursty workloads. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: a stripe-based prefetcher that issues clustered prefetch ahead-of-use, and a light-weight per-CPU pin highway that serializes pin/unpin bookkeeping per core to avoid global freelist races.

Design summary: stripe-prefetcher: maintains short-lived 'stripes' (small contiguous sets of blocks) discovered by scanning hot prefixes and allocation traces. Prefetch issues are batched into a vector-friendly path that emits contiguous async IO/KV-loads to warm the cache and prime KV block pin state. Prefetch budget is adjustable per-tenant and per-route; aggressive mode is disabled by default.

per-CPU pin highways: instead of a single freelist hot path with atomic handoffs, pins/unpins are shuttled through a per-CPU ring (highway) which batches releases and performs coalesced freelist returns. This reduces CAS storms on the global freelist and keeps hot allocations local to the CPU that consumed them. A global slowpath remains for cross-core steals.

Kernel-friendly hints: prefetcher emits 'kernel hints' that are consumed by the serving runtime path to select a vectorized copy kernel when contiguous stripes are available; this reduces per-block bookkeeping overhead when moving KV payloads into GPU-visible memory. The runtime selects the hint-aware kernel only when contiguous runs exceed a threshold to avoid fragmentation penalties.

Backward compatibility and safety: no on-disk format changes. Feature gated behind two runtime flags (kv.stripe_prefetcher.enabled, kv.percpu_pin.highways_enabled) and a dynamic prefetch_budget param. If either flag is disabled, behavior falls back to the existing allocator. We added a runtime guard to disable prefetch on constrained memory nodes and a throttler for background prefetch work to preserve latency SLOs.

Benchmarks: microbenchmarks on a 32-vCPU canary with 4 A100s show: +12% aggregate throughput for mixed small/med gen workloads, p99 latency down 18% on short-response chat-style requests, and a 22% reduction in CAS contention observed on the global freelist counter. End-to-end cost-per-token reduced ~6% under synthetic steady-state due to fewer reissued cache misses. Detailed numbers and methodology are in docs/ops/prefetcher.md.

Testing and rollout: unit and integration tests added; bench harness extended with a 'stripe' scenario. Rollout plan: gated canary -> region grayscale -> global enable with telemetry thresholds. Feature flags are on by default only for internal dev clusters.

Checklist:

- [x] Integration tests covering prefetch budget and disable guards

- [x] Telemetry (contention, prefetch hits/misses, highway occupancy)
- [x] Docs: ops guide and rollout notes

Related: ENG-4821 (allocator contention reduction), ENG-4923 (prefetch controls and telemetry).
